gold.question: Consider the transmitter that feeds controller FIC-11-1. When the transmitter fails, does the output go high or low, and how do I change that alarm direction?

candidate: The transmitter feeding FIC-11-1 is a Rosemount 3051 (FT-11-1). Its failure direction is not fixed — it is user-selectable. The factory default is a HIGH alarm (HART 4-20 mA output driven to ≥21.75 mA, or ≥22.5 mA for NAMUR/some option codes). To change it, you set the alarm direction with a jumper/switch on the transmitter (for output code A, HART 4-20 mA) or with an internal jumper (for the low-power output code M, which drives below 0.94 V for low alarm or above 5.4 V for high alarm). It can also be specified at ordering via alarm-level option codes: C4 (NAMUR, alarm high), CN (NAMUR, alarm low), CR/CS (custom high/low), CT (Rosemount standard low). Note: the datasheet describes only the jumper/switch method for changing the fail direction; software-menu configuration is not stated. Alarm current levels: default high ≥21.75 mA / low ≤3.75 mA; NAMUR high ≥22.5 mA / low ≤3.6 mA; custom high 20.2–23.0 mA, low 3.6–3.8 mA.
